speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) what is the median rent for hawker stalls tendered out in the last two years, excluding stalls that have had their rents adjusted after their three-year tenancy period; and (b) whether the National Environment Agency has any plans to review the duration of the initial tenancy period to discourage disproportionately high rental bids.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) when did the National Environment Agency last review the way hawker stalls are tendered out; (b) whether a ballot model at a fixed rental rate targeted at cost-recovery have been considered; and (c) if so, what are the reasons for not moving to such a model.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The National Environment Agency (NEA) lets out vacant hawker stalls through monthly tender exercises, which are transparent and fair.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: After the first tenancy term of three years, tendered stalls are adjusted towards an assessed market rent determined through independent professional valuation.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Since 2012, NEA has removed reserve rent and does not set a minimum bid price for hawker stall tenders.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As such, tenderers can secure stalls at lower-than-market rent for the first tenancy term.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This would not be attainable under a model where stalls are allocated at fixed rental rates.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: While some stalls at popular locations have attracted higher bids, such tender prices are not the norm.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: NEA is reviewing relevant policies at hawker centres to ensure that the system remains effective while keeping hawker food prices affordable.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Hawkers face various cost pressures, such as raw material and manpower costs.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: To address manpower challenges, NEA has provided support through measures, such as the Productive Hawker Centres programme and the Hawkers' Productivity Grant to help stallholders improve productivity and reduce reliance on manpower.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We are also looking at other ways to further ease manpower challenges.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Currently, only Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents can be stallholders or work as stall assistants in hawker centres managed by NEA and NEA-appointed operators.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: These measures help to safeguard and preserve the local identity of our hawker centres.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: NEA exercises some flexibility by allowing stallholders to appoint their spouses who are Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) or LTVP+ holders with a Letter of Consent (LOC) or Pre-approved LOC as their stall assistants, given their familial ties to the hawkers.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This policy will be effective from 1 January 2025.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This suggestion was also previously raised by Mr Edward Chia in an earlier Parliamentary Question.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I hope he will be happy that NEA is now making this move.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We are also studying other support measures for hawkers and will share the details when ready.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: (In Mandarin):   Hawkers face various cost pressures such as raw material and manpower cost.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Currently, only Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents can be stallholders or work as stall assistants in hawker centres managed by NEA and NEA-appointed operators.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: These measures help to safeguard and preserve the local identity of our hawker culture.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: NEA also allows stallholders to appoint their spouses who are LTVP or LTVP+ holders with a LOC or Pre-approved LOC as their stall assistants.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: To provide additional support to stallholders at hawker centres to manage manpower challenges, we will further relax our policy to allow hawkers to hire LTVP or LTVP+ holders with LOCs or Pre-approved LOCs to work as their stall assistants.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This policy will be effective from 1 January 2025.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We are also studying other support measures for hawkers and will share the details when ready.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: They shared that it is common that these hawkers would, therefore, have to charge higher food prices to make up for the high costs.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In some cases, other hawkers in the same hawker centre would then see this and take this as a signal that they can also increase their food prices, therefore, causing a price increase ripple within the same hawker centre.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: My first question is: does the Ministry track if food prices have, indeed, increased in hawker centres where there had been an abnormally high rental bid?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: My second question is: could the Ministry consider modelling its tender bid system after the Housing and Development Board's (HDB's) resale portal and alert prospective bidders if the rental bid that they have submitted exceeds the median rent in the same hawker centre, by say, about 10%?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Doing so can possibly help prospective hawkers place more realistic bids, but more importantly, I hope that this can help moderate food price increases as a result of high rental bids.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: On his first question of whether NEA tracks hawker food prices in correlation to the rental they bid for, I do not have the data at hand.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But I would say that in a price competitive market, in a hawker centre where there are multiple stalls offering food of different prices and different choices for consumers, it would be something that the market will have to take into account.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In other words, a person who bid for a high rental price at the stall, will have to take into account what consumers can bear as well, so that he can keep his business viable.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I think we have to allow the market to weed out those who are not competitive and unable to offer food at affordable prices where consumers will see this as good value for money, and allow some churn in the market so that at some point, the best operator with the best offering, in terms of taste and quality of the food with the price that consumers can bear, will be the one that eventually can succeed.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Having said that, I must emphasise that high stall rental bids that the Member may be talking about are actually the outliers and not the norm.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As in my reply earlier, the median cost of rental across our hawker centres has remained quite stable over the last few years.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And to ensure his longer-term viability, he would then have to be a bit more moderate about what kind of price he wants to bid for a stall.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I think this is something that NEA would take back and see how much more granular information we can put out.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Like I said, these are very rare circumstances where a small number or percentage of stallholders put in that kind of bid prices.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I would say most hawkers do try to make sure that they bid at a price that is sustainable for their own businesses.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And I think this is something that we will see how to enhance further.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: These disproportionally high rental rates do go against the intent of why we set up hawker centres, which is to provide hawker food at affordable prices.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State whether NEA, besides looking at the rental bids, could also do some due diligence on the bidders on whether they have the ability and the financial capacity to sustain at this kind of high rentals for their business, and because to take up a stall when another stallholder might have been able to do it better — so, very much like how, in public tenders, we look at price and quality, whether these stallholders have the means and capability to be able to sustain at such a high rental rate.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Indeed, I think it is always good to help the stall owners make a more considered bid when it comes to bidding for a stall.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But I would be cautious about putting in requirements that would make it much more difficult for a potential tenderer to put in a bid.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: When we say "doing due diligence", I think it could mean that we are going to impose a lot more onerous demands on the stall bidder to show a lot more information before we select the bid.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And that itself could disadvantage hawkers who may not be able to put in, say, a certain proposal or show their financial standing.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We do have to let the market, in some ways, select out those who can survive in a competitive marketplace.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Bear in mind that in a typical hawker centre, it is not everyone who will be in the outlier pricing, and as I have said, these are a small number of stalls in the grand scheme of things.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, by and large, the kind of hawker offerings in a particular hawker centre will help to moderate prices of other stalls who may find that it is difficult for them to survive if they were to actually price themselves out the market.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: When we talk about "due diligence", I think it is putting out more information, so that they can also be clear about what they are bidding for.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But, in fact, this is a very small number of bids that go into this kind of stratospheric range.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Because we still want to preserve the hawker culture, which is largely run by local Singaporeans, of course, with a small supplement from some LTVP+ LOC holders.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For example, with the grant, they can purchase food preparation processing equipment to do the meat mincing, vegetable chopping and also reduce their reliance on manpower to do these repetitive tasks.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, I think with these kinds of measures, we want hawkers to adopt a more productive approach to their business to be more sustainable, while for those who may still need some manpower, this is where the LTVP+ LOC liberalisation will help them to access some of these LTVP+ holders who are already here in Singapore on a permanent basis as part of a family nexus in Singapore, to be able to contribute economically as well.
